content.user_title: Review Code for Security and Quality
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, performance, and reliability issues. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured rules and clear findings.
actual_capabilities: Reviews code for SQL injection and XSS risks using dedicated security rules.
Identifies N+1 query patterns in ORM, GraphQL, and database access code.
Checks error handling, naming, type hints, and test coverage expectations.
Prioritizes review findings by critical, high, medium, and low severity.
Formats review output with issue, impact, fix, and summary sections.
Provides category-specific rule references for deeper review guidance.
limitations: It does not run tests or static analyzers unless the user provides those tools.
It needs source code or a pull request diff to produce concrete findings.
It cannot prove runtime behavior without application context and dependencies.
Its examples include intentionally vulnerable snippets for reviewer education.

use_cases.title: Audit Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Review pull request changes for security bugs, error handling gaps, and missing tests before merge.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Reviews
use_cases.description: Run a structured pre-release review that ranks blockers and follow-up work by severity.

use_cases.title: Coach Review Quality
use_cases.description: Teach consistent review habits with focused rules for security, performance, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for correctness, security, and maintainability. List findings by severity and include concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the attached pull request. Focus first on SQL injection, XSS, N+1 queries, and error handling. Note missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this change for security issues. Prioritize authentication, authorization, SQL injection, XSS, secrets, and unsafe input handling.

prompt_templates.title: Release Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release gate review. Identify merge blockers, high-risk regressions, performance risks, and required tests before deployment.

output_examples.input: Review a user lookup endpoint that builds SQL with a request parameter.
output: Critical: The query construction allows SQL injection through user-controlled input.
Fix: Use a parameterized query or an ORM filter that binds values safely.
Add tests for malicious input and missing users.

output_examples.input: Review a posts page that loads each author inside a loop.
output: High: The page has an N+1 query pattern that scales poorly with post count.
Fix: Use eager loading, a join, or batched author lookup.
Add a performance test or query count assertion for the list view.

output_examples.input: Review a frontend change that renders profile text into HTML.
output: Critical: Unsanitized HTML rendering can allow cross-site scripting.
Fix: Render plain text by default, or sanitize trusted HTML with a vetted library.
Add tests that cover dangerous markup and expected escaping.

best_practices: Review security issues before performance and maintainability feedback.
Cite exact files and lines for every actionable finding.
Separate confirmed defects from suggestions and style preferences.
anti_patterns: Do not mark educational examples as active vulnerabilities without context.
Do not hide critical security findings in a general summary.
Do not request broad refactors when a focused fix is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews code for security, performance, correctness, maintainability, and testing concerns.

faq.question: Does it execute my code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides review guidance and does not execute code by itself.

faq.question: Which security risks does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded secrets, and missing authorization checks.

faq.question: Can it review pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the diff or changed files so findings can reference exact locations.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It helps reviewers find issues, but humans should verify context and risk.

faq.question: Why are there vulnerable examples in the files?
faq.answer: They are teaching examples that show reviewers what unsafe patterns look like.
